whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the incident, though claims against a government entity can require action in as little as six months. Waiting too long can mean losing the right to seek compensation altogether.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. This means compensation isn't automatically capped just because your injuries aren't purely financial.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you win your case. This lets injured people pursue a claim without worrying about hourly rates or retainer costs.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in La Verne?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If a government entity is involved, such as a city vehicle or a hazard on public property, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking your situation quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't barred entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in La Verne?
items.answer: Public crash records point to higher collision counts along Foothill Boulevard, the SR-210 Foothill Freeway, Arrow Highway, and White Avenue. Reported crashes also tend to peak on Thursdays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m., though these are neutral counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm ourselves. We simply help connect injured people with an independent attorney, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most ordinary personal injury cases in California, there's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. This differs from some other states and can matter significantly depending on the nature of your injuries.
